title: Sonakshi Sinha Just Got Called India's Meryl Streep — and Her New Courtroom Drama Drops Globally This Friday
excerpt: 'System' pairs Sonakshi with Tamil superstar Jyotika in a legal thriller about privilege, power, and whether justice actually works. Available on Prime Video in 240+ countries from May 22.
body:
Director Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari just called Sonakshi Sinha the "Meryl Streep of our country." That's either hyperbole or prophecy — and *System*, arriving on Amazon Prime Video this Friday, May 22, might tell us which.

The film pairs Sonakshi with **Jyotika** — one of Tamil cinema's biggest names making her Hindi film debut — in a courtroom drama that asks a question every Indian who's dealt with the legal system already knows the answer to: *Does power shape the truth?*

## The Setup: Ten Cases, One Partnership

Sonakshi plays **Neha Rajvansh**, a young public prosecutor from a privileged background. Her father, played by **Ashutosh Gowariker** (yes, the *Lagaan* director, acting), runs a prestigious law firm. To earn a partnership — not inherit it, earn it — Neha must win ten consecutive cases.

She wins nine.

The tenth is the one that breaks the formula. It's the case that forces her to confront whether the system she's been mastering is actually just, or whether she's been playing a rigged game with her father's name as the cheat code.

Enter **Sarika Rawat**, played by Jyotika — a street-smart courtroom stenographer who's recorded hundreds of verdicts without ever having the luxury of being the one who delivers them. Neha recruits her for the final case, but Sarika has her own motives, her own grievances against a system that types women like her into the footnotes.

## Why Jyotika's Hindi Debut Matters

Jyotika is not a newcomer crossing over for visibility. She's a superstar in Tamil Nadu — the woman who headlined *36 Vayadhinile*, *Ponmagal Vandhal*, and *Pon Ondru Kanden*, films where she carried the entire narrative without a male lead to lean on.

In a Bollywood Hungama interview, Jyotika said she was drawn to *System* because the role required her to be "very proudly and boldly" invisible — a stenographer who sees everything but is seen by no one. *"It's more comforting to work with a female filmmaker,"* she added, *"because the emotional layering is understood without having to explain it."*

For Tamil cinema fans in the US and UK who've followed Jyotika for two decades, seeing her in a Hindi film from a director as deliberate as Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari is a crossover that actually means something.

## Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari's Anti-Reel Approach

The director of *Nil Battey Sannata* and *Bareilly Ki Barfi* told **Hollywood Reporter India** that *System* deliberately rejects the fast-cutting, reel-friendly editing style that's taken over Indian streaming. The film breathes. It lets courtroom scenes play out in near-real-time. It trusts its actors to hold a frame.

*"This isn't about pace,"* Tiwari said. *"It's about stillness. The most powerful moments in a courtroom happen in silence — when someone realizes the truth and decides whether to say it."*

She described the film as an exploration of "generational karma" — the idea that privilege isn't earned or deserved, it's simply passed down, and the institutions that enforce it call that process justice.

## Streaming Globally on Day One

*System* premieres **May 22 on Amazon Prime Video** — available simultaneously across India and **240+ countries and territories**. No theatrical window. No geo-restrictions. If you have a Prime subscription in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, or the Gulf, it's there on Friday.

For NRIs who left India partly because the system didn't feel navigable — because it rewarded last names over merit, connections over competence — this film might feel less like entertainment and more like therapy.

Or at least a very well-acted version of that family dinner argument you've been having for years.

*System. Directed by Ashwiny Iyer Tiwari. Starring Sonakshi Sinha, Jyotika, Ashutosh Gowariker. Premieres May 22, 2026, on Amazon Prime Video worldwide.*
